subject: ela
intro: Students retell a story's beginning, middle, and end using key details, and then identify the central message or lesson the story teaches. This skill builds comprehension and helps students see the deeper meaning behind a story.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

A little turtle wanted to cross the road. He walked slowly. A girl named Maya saw him and waited. She made sure no cars came. The turtle made it safely to the other side.

Retell the story. Tell what happened at the beginning, middle, and end.

steps: I think: what happened first? A turtle wanted to cross the road.
What happened in the middle? Maya saw him and waited. She made sure no cars came.
What happened at the end? The turtle made it safely across.
I put it together in order.
solution.answer: At the beginning, a little turtle wanted to cross the road. In the middle, Maya saw him and helped by watching for cars. At the end, the turtle got safely to the other side.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Leo had one cookie left. His friend Aisha looked hungry. Leo thought about eating it himself. Then he broke it in half and shared it with Aisha. Aisha smiled.

What is the central message of this story?

steps: I ask: what did the character learn or what lesson does this story teach?
Leo almost kept the cookie but chose to share.
Sharing made Aisha smile, which was a good outcome.
The lesson is about sharing and thinking of others.
solution.answer: The central message is that sharing with others makes everyone feel good.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Sam wanted to build a tall tower with blocks. The first tower fell down. He tried again. That tower fell too. He tried a third time, moving slowly and carefully. This tower stood tall.

Retell this story in your own words.

steps: Beginning: Sam tried to build a tower and it fell.
Middle: He tried again and it fell again.
End: He went slowly and carefully, and the third tower stood tall.
solution.answer: Sam tried to build a block tower, but it fell down twice. He kept trying and was careful on his third try. Finally his tower stood tall.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

A small ant found a big crumb of bread. She could not carry it alone. She called to her ant friends. Together, they all carried the crumb back to the ant hill.

What is the central message of this story?

steps: I ask: what lesson does this story teach?
The ant could not do it alone.
When her friends helped, they succeeded.
The message is about teamwork.
solution.answer: The central message is that working together helps you do things you cannot do alone.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Zoe told a lie to get out of trouble. Her mom found out the truth later. Her mom was more upset about the lie than the original problem. Zoe felt very sorry.

Retell the story and tell what lesson Zoe learned.

steps: Beginning: Zoe told a lie to avoid getting in trouble.
Middle: Her mom found out the lie.
End: Her mom was more upset about the lie, and Zoe felt sorry.
Lesson: Lying makes things worse.
solution.answer: Zoe told a lie to stay out of trouble. Her mom found out and was very upset. Zoe learned that lying makes things worse than just telling the truth.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Ben found a baby bird on the ground. He put it in a box with a soft towel. He gave it water with a dropper. Every day he took care of it. One morning, the bird flew away on its own.

Retell this story using beginning, middle, and end.
items.hint: Think about what Ben found, what he did, and what happened at the end.

steps: Beginning: Ben found a baby bird on the ground.
Middle: He took care of it every day, giving it a safe place and water.
End: The bird got better and flew away.
solution.answer: At the beginning, Ben found a baby bird on the ground. In the middle, he took care of it every day by giving it a home and water. At the end, the bird was strong enough to fly away on its own.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Marco had a new toy car. His little sister asked to play with it. Marco said no. He went to his room and played alone. He did not feel happy. Later, he let her play too, and they had a great time.

What is the central message of this story?
items.hint: Look at what made Marco happy at the end. What changed?

steps: When Marco refused to share, he felt unhappy.
When he shared, they both had a great time.
The lesson is about sharing and how it feels better to include others.
solution.answer: The central message is that sharing brings more joy than keeping things to yourself.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Maya rushed through her homework. She made many mistakes. Her teacher handed it back with red marks. That night, Maya slowed down and did it again carefully. She got every answer right.

What lesson did Maya learn? Use details from the story.
items.hint: What happened when she rushed? What happened when she was careful?

steps: When Maya rushed, she made mistakes.
When she slowed down and was careful, she got everything right.
The lesson is about taking your time.
solution.answer: Maya learned that it is important to slow down and be careful with your work. Rushing leads to mistakes, but taking your time leads to success.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Aisha was scared to try the big slide at the park. She watched other kids go down. She climbed the steps slowly. She slid down and landed with a big smile. She went up again right away.

Retell this story in order.
items.hint: Think about what Aisha did first, next, and last.

steps: Beginning: Aisha was scared of the big slide.
Middle: She watched other kids and then climbed up slowly.
End: She slid down, smiled, and went back up again.
solution.answer: At first, Aisha was scared of the big slide. Then she watched others and slowly climbed up. When she slid down and landed, she was so happy she went up and did it again.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Leo made fun of a boy named Omar who had a funny lunch. Omar sat alone and looked sad. Leo did not feel good about what he said. After school, Leo went over and said sorry. Omar smiled and said it was okay.

What is the central message of this story?
items.hint: Think about how Leo felt and what he did to fix things.

steps: Leo said something unkind and it hurt Omar.
Leo felt bad and apologized.
The story shows the importance of kindness and saying sorry when you are wrong.
solution.answer: The central message is that we should be kind to others, and when we make a mistake, we should apologize.
